# Synapse 2.1.2

Synapse AI now tries each plan once on made-up answers before you see it, and catches more of what a plan reads and wouldn't get. A knowledge base reads pages that only JavaScript writes, and a card that waits on another comes up as soon as you press the one before it.

## Changed

- **A plan is tried once on made-up answers before you see it.** The plan check judged what a step reads only against what the steps before it say they answer, so it couldn't see what a code step makes, or a read deep inside an answer: the run found those. Now, before the card, the plan runs once on made-up answers in each step's declared shape, with its code run and no model, no tool, no network and nothing saved. A step that reads what it wouldn't get goes back to Synapse AI to fix, and one still there after that is said on the card, never a block. Code is tried only where it can be kept off the network; where it can't (the host runtime, or no Docker), the card says which step wasn't tried.
- **A knowledge base reads a page whose words only JavaScript writes.** Such a page was left out with words that said it may need JavaScript. Where Chromium is installed, Knowledge now renders it once, still as SynapseBot, and indexes its words. It never takes a browser check: a page that answered 403 or a challenge is never rendered, and one that lands on a sign-in page says it needs a sign-in. A crawl renders at most 20 pages; without Chromium, nothing changes.
- **A card that waits on another comes up as soon as you press it.** Asked for a knowledge base with a note in it, Synapse AI put up the card to make the base and said the note would come once it was made: press Make it, then ask again. Now the note's card comes up right under it as soon as Make it works, ready to press; the same goes for a board's comment or access. A change that needs your review, such as a new base's settings, still asks you to ask again once it's made.

## Fixed

- **A step that reads a tool's whole answer says which fields it uses.** A step could read everything a tool answered and assume a field it doesn't have, such as humidity from a tool that answers only the city and the temperature, and nothing caught it, because no field was named. Now a step that reads the whole answer of a tool that declares its answer names the fields it uses, and each is checked against what the tool says it answers; if it still names none, the plan says that step's use of the answer isn't checked. A field written in a step's prompt as code, such as `find.humidity`, is checked the same way.
- **Code that reads a table's rows goes through its rows.** A plan's code could go through a page read's whole answer, which walks its field names, so the rows it read became an empty file. The plan check now sends that back with the field to read (a table's `data`), and the editor warns of it.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.1.2`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.1.1, 2.1.0 or 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first. From 2.1.0 or 2.0.x, the [2.1.1 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.1.1) say what changed there too, such as `synapse stop`'s two lines.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.
